cards.title: The scams that target Papa's worries
cards.body: Elders get 'miracle cure' forwards, fake doctor calls and too-good offers. They play on real health fears, which makes them convincing.

cards.title: Miracle cures in forwarded messages
cards.body: 'Leave BP tablets forever with this kadha.' Any message telling someone to stop prescribed medicine is a red flag. Check with the doctor first.

cards.title: Calls asking for OTPs or card details
cards.body: No genuine hospital, insurer or lab needs your OTP over a call. Hang up and call the official number yourself.

cards.title: Fake free health camps and tests
cards.body: Offers asking for advance payment, Aadhaar or bank details for a 'free' check-up are suspicious. Verify with a known local clinic.

cards.title: Medicines sold through calls or links
cards.body: Cheap medicine offers through random links or calls can mean fake products. Buy from a known chemist and take a proper bill.

cards.title: Pressure is the biggest giveaway
cards.body: 'Offer ends today', 'your policy will lapse', 'act now'. Real health services don't rush people. Urgency is a scammer's favourite tool.

cards.title: Make a 'call me first' rule
cards.body: Agree with your parents: before paying, sharing details or changing medicines because of a message, they call you. Report cyber fraud on 1930.

takeaway: Miracle cures, OTP calls, fake camps and pushy offers are red flags. Agree on a 'call me first' rule with parents.
share: Tell Mummy Papa: no real hospital asks for an OTP. Call me first before paying or sharing anything.
